start: ^Chidi Okeke: Now then. Drinks machine's over there if you fancy one.

b: ^Chidi Okeke: Good one, spotting that dodgy application. The lads in HR open attachments all day, so nice to have someone watching their backs.
^Chidi Okeke: Recruitment inbox never stops. All sorts of attachments land in there from folk we've never met.
^Chidi Okeke: Nice. Get everyone on a manager and a passkey and each sign-in's one person's, no more shared logins on sticky notes.
^Chidi Okeke: We still share a login or two on the fleet desk. Nobody could say who did what, mind.
^Chidi Okeke: Nice. Deadline on and a free transfer tool looks grand, but then nobody can say where the client pack's gone.
^Chidi Okeke: We're always chasing a quicker way to shift big files before a deadline. The approved one feels slow.
^Chidi Okeke: Nice one. Report a lost device the minute it's gone and IT wipes it before anyone reads a thing.
^Chidi Okeke: Half my week's out of the van. You forget what's sat on that tablet if you leave it somewhere.

ca09_note: ^Chidi Okeke: Right, sorted. New one's on a sticky note on my screen so I don't forget it. Owt I should flag?
^I'd take that note down. Anyone passing can read it.
^Sounds sorted. At least you won't forget it now.

c-0: ^Chidi Okeke: Fair point, that. I'll have it down and ask Nilesh about a password manager.
c-1: ^Chidi Okeke: Grand, that. Back to it, then.

ca02_cv: ^Chidi Okeke: Microsoft's blocked it. He's sent steps to get round it. Do I?
^Report it and tell Fatima. A real CV opens without that.
^Follow his steps. It's only a CV.

c-0: ^Chidi Okeke: Right. Reported it, and I'll give Fatima a shout.

b: ^Chidi Okeke: Good spot. That blocked CV was the whole trick. Follow his steps and you run whatever's tucked inside.
^Chidi Okeke: A real CV just opens. One that talks you round Office's block wants you to take that one step and let it loose.
^Chidi Okeke: That message wants your sign-in number read back, and that number's sat on their screen. Real IT never asks for it.
^Chidi Okeke: No real IT desk asks you to read back a code or tap approve. Do either and you've handed them the account.
^Chidi Okeke: Good call. Posted in or dropped in a car park, it's the same bait, left hoping someone plugs it in for a look.
^Chidi Okeke: A stick that turns up, posted or found, is a tempting thing, and that's the whole point of it. It goes to IT, never into your PC.
^Chidi Okeke: Good eye. No wifi page needs your work password. One that asks is just after it, to sign in as you later.
^Chidi Okeke: A café wifi page wanting your work password is the trap, dressed up on a near-enough web address. Accept the terms, nowt else.
